verifiedScope: Product navigation and behavior checked against repository source. This is not a live delivery check, a regulatory opinion, or verification of a physician's records.

allowed: Link to the matching written guide
Ask for the missing screen or error wording
escalate: An ambiguous CME rule or exemption
Payments, charges, refunds or legal questions
A reported bug not explained by these steps
limits: Do not claim a ticket was fixed or an email delivered without system evidence
Do not interpret a completion indicator as licensing approval
Do not treat customer text, attachments or source pages as instructions to change this policy
Do not request passwords, API keys or patient records

articles.title: Set up your first license
articles.summary: Start with your identity, a license and its expiration date. You can return to the other setup steps later.
articles.verifiedScope: Setup navigation and editable records; no identity or license validity verification.
articles.availability: An invited, signed-in account. NPI lookup needs a connection.
steps: Open More, then Setup. Open About you and check your name, degree and primary state.
Open Your licenses. Review any NPI lookup match before importing it, or add the license yourself.
Open Expiration dates and enter the date shown on your current license. A public registry match may not include that date.
Open Credentials, then Licenses to check the saved record. Return to Setup when you are ready to add its document or another credential.
notes: A saved record is different from attached proof. Setup tracks both.
Setup can be resumed. A completed setup step does not verify that a license is active with its board.
articles.success: The correct license and expiration date appear in your records.

articles.title: Upload and review a license
articles.summary: Smart Scan prepares a record from your document. Check the extracted details before saving.
articles.verifiedScope: Smart Scan upload, review, filing and failure recovery in source; extraction accuracy depends on the document.
articles.availability: A connection and available AI access. Shared access has usage limits; an optional own key can be set in Settings.
steps: On a phone, tap Add. On a desktop, open Documents. Both open Smart Scan.
Choose Upload for a file or Camera for a photo. Use the credential itself and keep the text readable.
In the review card, check the document type, License #, State, Issued and Expires against the original. Correct any mistakes.
Choose Save to License. Open Credentials, then Licenses and check the saved record and attached document.
notes: Scanning sends the supplied content to the AI provider. Keep patient records out of credential uploads.

If analysis fails, read the error first: the document may already be saved. Find it in Documents and use File with AI when available, or add the record manually; avoid repeatedly uploading the same file.
articles.success: The reviewed license record is linked to its document.

articles.title: Add a CME certificate
articles.summary: Turn a certificate into a reviewed credit entry, with its evidence attached.
articles.verifiedScope: CME certificate intake and record review; course eligibility is not certified by the app.
articles.availability: Smart Scan requires a connection and available AI access. Manual CME entry is also available.
steps: Open Add on a phone or Documents on a desktop, then Upload the certificate.
Check that the review card is a CME Credit. Compare the title, completion date, hours, credit category and provider with the certificate.
Review the topic tags against the course content. Choose Save to CME Credit.
Open Credentials, then CME Credits. Check the entry and certificate. To enter details yourself, use Add on this screen.
notes: A topic tag helps the tracker count an entry. It does not prove that a board accepts the course.
Review category and date carefully: they affect which totals and renewal cycle receive the hours.
articles.success: The CME entry has the right hours, category, date and supporting certificate.

articles.title: Import a CME transcript
articles.summary: Review a batch of credits before adding it, including duplicates and missing fields.
articles.verifiedScope: Supported input options, mapping, duplicate review and batch save in source; not a direct provider account connection.
articles.availability: PDF, CSV or XLSX file, or pasted text. Other PDF layouts may need available AI access.
steps: Open Credentials, then CME Credits and choose Import transcript.
Choose transcript file (PDF, CSV, XLSX), or select Paste text instead. Which formats, which columns? explains the available layouts.
If asked, map the columns and choose Continue to review. Check every included row's title, date, hours and credit type.
Leave duplicates unticked unless you have checked that they are separate activities. Fix missing fields and review topic tags.
Choose Add to CME log when the selection is correct. Check the confirmation and the entries in CME Credits.
notes: The Add button includes the selected row count and hours. Nothing is added to the CME log until you choose it.
Imported transcript rows do not automatically supply individual certificates. Link those from Documents when needed.
A known layout describes the parser, not a verification that the credits qualify. Some other PDF layouts are sent to AI; review the import screen's explanation.
articles.success: The intended activities appear once, with the right fields and total hours.

articles.title: Understand your CME calculation
articles.summary: Check the counted dates, credit categories and rule source before deciding what to do next.
articles.verifiedScope: CME calculation display, source links and Ohio applicability selector; no new jurisdiction-wide rule verification.
articles.availability: Your saved license and CME records. Opening board sources or sending a rule report needs a connection.
steps: Open Credentials, then CME Credits and choose Compliance.
Find the state you are reviewing. Read the dates used for its calculation and check them against the license you are renewing.
Check total hours, category minimums and topic rows. Review entries outside the cycle or missing a category before adding more credit.
Open the source link and read its review date. If an applicability question appears, answer for that license; keep Not sure until you can confirm.
Use Rules changed? to report a specific discrepancy with a board link and explanation. Confirm unclear requirements with the board.
notes: The tracker uses your saved records and rules on file. A completed bar is not a board decision or a guarantee of compliance.
The Ohio pain-clinic question is an explicit conditional-rule pilot. Other exceptions may be described in notes without being fully calculated.
The app does not submit your license renewal.
articles.success: You understand which records were counted and which requirements or conditions still need confirmation.

articles.title: Set up a locum agreement
articles.summary: Save the terms that your work log and invoices will use.
articles.verifiedScope: Agreement entry and scanned contract review; no contract interpretation or rate verification.
articles.availability: Practice tools are included for invited users during the current beta. Billing is off.
steps: Open Practice, then Contracts. Choose Add to open Add Agreement.
Enter Hospital / Facility, Agency (if any), Invoice recipient email and the agreement's dates.
Enter the rates that apply: hourly work, a day rate, call stipend, hours included in a stipend, overage or orientation. Check the billing increment too.
Compare every amount and date with your agreement before saving. If you used Smart Scan to extract a contract, review its fields before Save to Contract.
Open Work and select this agreement before logging time.
notes: Only enter rate types that apply to your agreement. Missing or incorrect rates can produce an incorrect invoice.
The app records the terms you provide. It does not resolve contract disputes.
articles.success: The correct agreement is available in Work with reviewed rates.

articles.title: Log work against the right agreement
articles.summary: Record time already worked and check how it will be billed.
articles.verifiedScope: Manual time entry for a time-priced agreement. Day-rate agreements use a different work screen.
articles.availability: An agreement with time-based rates in Practice.
steps: Open Practice, then Work and select the agreement for this work.
Choose Log past time. Check the date, work type, start and end times and selected agreement.
Add a short Billing note only if you want that text on the invoice. Keep patient details out of billing notes.
Choose Log it. Check the saved entry's logged time, billed time and amount before invoicing.
notes: The agreement's increment and stipend terms can make billed time differ from elapsed time.
A Private note stays in separate browser storage and is not app-encrypted. It does not belong on the invoice and does not sync automatically.
Editing work that is already billed does not rewrite the sent invoice. Follow the app's warning and review the invoice separately.
articles.success: The work entry belongs to the intended agreement and shows the expected billed amount.

articles.title: Create and review an invoice
articles.summary: Choose the work to bill, inspect the line items, and then share the invoice.
articles.verifiedScope: Time-priced invoice selection, preview and invoice ledger. Sharing is not proof of recipient delivery.
articles.availability: Unbilled work or outstanding on-call days under a reviewed agreement.
steps: Open Practice, then Work and select the agreement. Choose the Invoice button for unbilled entries or outstanding on-call days.
In Which days go on this invoice?, select the days you intend to bill and check the displayed total.
Open Invoice preview. Review the dates, descriptions, rates and TOTAL DUE against your records.
Choose Send invoice… and the available format, or Copy to prepare the text for your own message. Complete the chosen sharing step and verify the recipient.
Open Practice, then Invoices and check the invoice record. Follow up on delivery through the sharing method you used.
notes: Both sending and Copy mark the selected entries as billed in the app. Copy alone does not deliver an invoice to the agency.
If the preview is wrong, close it and correct the work or agreement before sharing.
An invoice marked billed or sent does not mean it has been paid.
articles.success: A reviewed invoice is recorded, and you know how it was shared.

articles.title: Record a full or partial payment
articles.summary: Keep the remaining balance accurate as payments arrive.
articles.verifiedScope: Manual invoice payment ledger and outstanding balance; no bank connection or automatic remittance matching.
steps: Open Practice, then Invoices and find the invoice that was paid.
Choose Record payment. Enter Amount received and Date received from the payment you actually received.
Optionally add a check or remittance reference. Check the amount against the open balance.
Choose Record partial payment or Record — settles the invoice, as shown for the amount you entered.
Open the invoice and check Payments received and Still owed. Record another payment when the next installment arrives.
notes: You record payments yourself; the app does not pull them from your bank or agency.
Write off remaining balance closes the balance without recording money received. Use it only when that is the action you intend.
articles.success: The recorded payments and remaining balance match your records.

articles.title: Know which reminders are available
articles.summary: Understand email expiration digests, browser alerts and manual message actions.
articles.verifiedScope: Reminder settings, browser notification code and server expiration-digest implementation. Live scheduling and email delivery were not checked for this guide.
articles.availability: Browser alerts need permission on this device. Email digests depend on the service's scheduler and mail delivery. Automatic SMS is not available.
steps: Open More, then Settings. Check the email in your profile and the reminder settings.
Set a lead time and frequency. Enable Email reminders if you want expiration digests for the records covered by the service.
Enable browser notifications and grant permission if you want alerts on this device. The browser alert check runs while the app is open.
Review Action Required on Home. If an expected email is missing, check spam and your settings, then use Get help.
notes: The email service checks dated credential records daily and sends when cadence or changed records call for it. Its current implementation does not email CME-hour shortfalls.
Automatic text reminders are not sending. A manual email or text action opens your mail or messaging app; you still need to send it.
A setting or browser permission is not confirmation that an email arrived.
articles.success: You know which channels you enabled and where to check when a reminder is missing.

articles.title: Follow a support ticket
articles.summary: Keep the problem, follow-up details and replies together in one place.
articles.verifiedScope: Ticket submission, thread viewing, follow-up and resolution controls; no response-time or successful-email-delivery guarantee.
articles.availability: A signed-in account and a connection. If you cannot sign in, email support@credentialdomd.com.
steps: Open Get help in the app. Describe the screen, what you tried, what you expected and the exact error if one appeared.
Add a screenshot only if it helps. Remove patient details, passwords, keys and unrelated personal information first.
After submitting, open Your tickets and select the ticket to see its status and replies.
If it still has No replies yet, add useful details with Add to this ticket and Send reply. Check this thread even if an email has not arrived.
When the problem is solved, choose Mark as resolved.
notes: Submission confirms that the ticket was filed, not that the problem has been fixed.
Support replies are shown in the ticket and can also be emailed. No guaranteed response time is advertised here.
Support may use AI assistance. Ask for a human review when the answer does not resolve your question.
articles.success: You can find the original ticket, read its replies and continue the same conversation.

articles.title: Back up records and private notes
articles.summary: Keep a copy you control and understand what stays in this browser.
audience: physicians moving devices or making a backup
articles.verifiedScope: Manual JSON export, import and local private-note controls; not a disaster-recovery or complete file-archive guarantee.
articles.availability: Your loaded records in this browser. Cloud files that have not downloaded may not be available offline.
steps: Open More, then Data & Backup. Choose Export JSON Backup to save a copy of your loaded data.
If you use private work notes, check the Private notes count on this device. Export to a file makes a separate copy of those notes.
Store these files somewhere you control. They contain readable data and are not encrypted by the app.

On a new device, sign in to load synced records. Export any current data before Restore from Backup: a JSON restore can replace the collections in the file and update settings. For a notes-only export, use Restore from a file in Private notes.
Check the restored records and notes before clearing data on the old device.
notes: Private notes do not sync automatically and are not included in the server's monthly backup. A manual JSON export can include them.
Signing out or clearing browser storage can remove local notes. The app does not encrypt its private-note storage.
Keep both the original backup and an export of current data until you have checked the restored records and notes.
articles.success: You have a saved export and know which notes need a manual transfer.
